open_points.subject: canonical_values.json_depth
open_points.text: “One JSON text as its UTF-8 bytes, well-formed or not.” / “a text that is not JSON is measured all the same”
open_points.question: What depth must json_depth return for malformed JSON, including unmatched containers, truncated strings, invalid escapes, trailing material, or bytes that are not valid UTF-8?
options: Count structurally significant brackets while lexing and define explicit rules for every malformed form
Return the maximum depth reached before the first lexical or syntactic error
Return an invalid-text result instead of a depth
open_points.default_guess: Lex the bytes non-recursively, ignore brackets inside recognized strings, and return the maximum structural depth reached even if the text is malformed.

open_points.subject: installation.load_installation
open_points.text: State 4 says “its depth, measured before it is parsed with capability:canonical_values.json_depth ... within json_depth_max”, while State 5 says “Checks in this order ... a regular private file ...; one JSON object with exactly the installation's fields” and omits any depth check.
open_points.question: Where exactly does the configuration depth check occur in load_installation's ordered checks, and what refusal reason names an over-depth file?
options: Insert a distinct depth check after the file check and before JSON parsing
Treat over-depth as failure of the existing “one JSON object” check while still measuring before parsing
Do not enforce depth in load_installation
open_points.default_guess: Insert the depth check after the regular-private-file check and before parsing, returning refused with a reason naming the depth limit.

open_points.subject: installation.current_token_list
open_points.text: A20 requires the installation configuration to be depth-bounded on a failed re-read path, but current_token_list enforces “the four checks only” and names only readability/parsing, token length, token uniqueness and agent-name uniqueness.
open_points.question: Must every changed configuration file be measured with json_depth before the token-list re-read parses it, and if it is too deep does current_token_list return no valid list under the existing parse check or under an additional fifth check?
options: Measure first and classify over-depth under the existing read-and-parse check
Add depth as a distinct fifth re-read check
Apply the depth limit only at startup, not token-list re-read
open_points.default_guess: Measure the entire changed file before parsing and treat over-depth as failure of the existing read-and-parse check, causing current_token_list to return none.
